Nine men's morris, side O. Game 1 starter brain (no past data yet).

Priorities each turn:
1. If a placement/move closes a mill, do it. Removal: prefer an opponent piece that (a) is part of a two-in-a-row with a free third point, or (b) has high mobility. Pieces in mills cannot be taken unless all are in mills.
2. If opponent has two on a line with the third point free, block it (unless we can mill first).
3. Early placement: take junction points 5, 11, 14, 20 (middle-square midpoints, 4 neighbours) and corners of the middle ring for mobility. Avoid outer corners early unless they make a mill threat.
4. Build double threats: place so one piece makes two pairs with free third points; opponent can block only one.
5. In the movement phase, keep pieces mobile; avoid moves that leave our two-in-a-row open for opponent to block; avoid letting our side get blocked (no legal move = loss).
6. With 3 pieces left, pieces may fly: keep a mill threat ready.
7. Draw watch: 40 turns without mill after placement, or 120 turns total. If behind, aim for repetition/draw.
Log after each game: which opening worked, which opponent patterns appeared, and whether the opponent blocked double threats.

args.text:
Nine men's morris, 2 residents per side (X and O teams). Brain v1 (untested draft).

PLACEMENT PHASE
- Priority order each turn: (1) close a mill if possible; (2) block an opponent two-in-a-line whose third point is free; (3) make your own two-in-a-line with a free third point (forcing the block); (4) occupy junction points with 4 neighbours: 5, 11, 14, 20 (then 8, 12, 13, 17 with 3 neighbours on the middle ring).
- Avoid placing pieces that can be trapped on corners (1, 3, 22, 24 have only 2 neighbours) unless they complete a mill.
- Keep pieces spread across different lines so one opponent block cannot kill two of our threats.

MOVEMENT PHASE
- Keep pieces mobile; prefer moves that open a line for a future mill (move a piece out of a mill and back in to re-close it = repeated captures).
- Before each move, check: after my move, can the opponent close a mill next turn? If yes, block it or make a counter-threat that is faster.
- Removal choice after our mill: remove an opponent piece that is part of an opponent two-in-a-line or that is highly mobile; never leave our own two-in-line exposed to an immediate block.

ENDGAME (3 pieces left, can fly)
- Count threats: a flying piece can block any point, so create two simultaneous threats (double attack) rather than one.

DRAWS
- Watch the 40-turn no-mill rule after placement and threefold repetition; if ahead in material, avoid repetition; if behind, repeat to draw.

PROCESS
- Captain proposes; team votes. Keep reasons short. Track the board with viewBoard before every move.
